channel.title: Standard Mobile Company Market Insights
channel.description: Research on IT asset disposition, refurbished electronics, and the secondary hardware market.

item.title: Apple’s Trade-In Bid Versus an Independent Wholesale Bid
item.description: Apple’s trade-in offer is a retail credit tied to a new purchase. An independent wholesale bid is cash for the device as inventory. How sellers and IT managers should compare the two.

item.title: How Fourth-Quarter Carrier Promotions Become January’s Wholesale Glut
item.description: Holiday carrier trade-in promotions pull phones out of pockets in October and November. Processing lag, grading queues, and liquidation calendars turn that surge into January wholesale supply.

item.title: Workstation GPUs Versus Data-Center GPUs on the Used Market
item.description: Used workstation GPUs and data-center GPUs clear through different buyers, form factors, and power constraints. How wholesale bids split between RTX professional cards and A100/H100-class accelerators.

item.title: What Changes When Used Equipment Crosses a Border With Data Still on It
item.description: Residual data on used laptops, servers, and phones becomes a multi-jurisdiction problem the moment the shipment clears customs. What changes for exporters, IT managers, and wholesale buyers.

item.title: Windows 11 Hardware Rules and the PCs That Cannot Follow
item.description: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, and a supported CPU. Machines that fail those checks leave managed Windows fleets and land in narrower wholesale channels.

item.title: The Chain-of-Custody File a Hardware Buyer Should Demand
item.description: Wholesale hardware without a usable chain-of-custody file is a liability transfer. What serials, wipe proofs, and handoff records a buyer should demand before the truck leaves.

item.title: Why Rising Rack Power Is Retiring Servers Early
item.description: Data centers are pulling still-working servers off the floor because rack power budgets, not failure rates, now set refresh timing. How that supply reaches wholesale.

item.title: What Copilot+ PCs Do to the Laptops They Replace
item.description: Copilot+ PC refreshes pull mid-cycle Windows 11 laptops into ITAD earlier, raise wholesale supply, and split secondary-market bids by NPU readiness. What buyers and IT managers should expect.

item.title: The Secondary Market for Optical Transceivers and SFP Modules
item.description: Used SFP, SFP+, QSFP, and QSFP28 optics clear as their own wholesale SKUs after network and storage refreshes. What buyers and IT managers should verify before bidding.

item.title: Used Enterprise Storage Arrays After a Refresh: Dell, NetApp, and Pure
item.description: After a storage refresh, Dell EMC, NetApp, and Pure arrays hit the secondary market as controllers, shelves, and media—not as turnkey systems. What buyers and IT managers should price.

item.title: Why Three-Year Lease Returns Set the Wholesale Price for Business Laptops
item.description: Corporate three-year lease returns flood the secondary market in predictable waves. Residual values, config mix, and return timing set wholesale bids for ThinkPads, Latitudes, and EliteBooks.

item.title: How Apple Silicon Macs Actually Depreciate, From M1 Through Later Chips
item.description: Apple silicon Macs do not depreciate like Intel Macs. Chip generation, unified-memory config, and macOS support length set wholesale bids from M1 through later M-series machines.

item.title: What Windows 10 End of Support Did to the Corporate PC Secondary Market
item.description: Microsoft ended Windows 10 support on October 14, 2025. That deadline flooded ITAD channels with business laptops, split the wholesale market by Windows 11 readiness, and reset prices for fleets that cannot upgrade.
